body: I'm sorry, I don't understand what you're asking. Can you tell me what you're doing, what you expected, and what actually happened?
i'm saying labels aren't being recognized for `for in` loops

sorry that may have been too meta... here's an example.  I expect the rule `no-empty-labels` to not have an error for this statement but it does:

``` js
label:
  for (var i in {}) {

  }
```

works for `while()` and `for` loops

issue.title: add; for-in support to no-empty-label rule

issue.body:
Labels on `for-in` loops were being marked as an error with the `no-empty-label` rule.  This fixes that.  Convo started in:

https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/1161

body: hey @nzakas, I just made a pr describing the issue and fix, let me know if you have any questions.  sorry for the confusion :(
Again, "aren't being recognized" doesn't give me enough information. Please tell me what you're expecting to happen and what actually happened.
I think it's pretty obvious from @wavded's descriptions: the for-in statement is being treated differently from other iteration statements by the `no-empty-label` rule, and should not be.

@michaelficarra the last comment I saw was the "aren't being recognized" one. For some reason, the other comments didn't show up for me when I was replying. The subsequent comments make it clear. 

Still, I'd like to remind everyone of what is expected when filing bugs. It's listed out quite explicitly in the contribution guide: http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing.html

@nzakas I've got that pull updated, my bad on the contributing guide, should have read more closely, this repo is the first that i've seen that has a commit message style.  i kinda like it, keeping things clean.
